claim_verdicts.evidence: git show stage-1:DonHang.Api/Middleware/ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs re-read today: catch (KeyNotFoundException ex) -> LogWarning(ex, "request for a resource that does not exist") + WriteProblemAsync(context, Status404NotFound, "Not found", ex.Message); catch (ArgumentException ex) -> LogWarning + Status400BadRequest, "Invalid request", ex.Message; catch (Exception ex) -> LogError(ex, "unhandled exception") + Status500InternalServerError, "Server error", "something went wrong". The lesson's code block is character-identical to lines 10-31 after whitespace normalisation.

C# language reference, verbatim: "When an exception occurs, the runtime checks catch clauses in the specified order, from top to bottom. At most, only one `catch` block runs for any thrown exception. ... A catch clause without any specified exception type matches any exception and, if present, must be the last catch clause."

git show stage-1:DonHang.Api/Program.cs, read today: app.UseMiddleware<ExceptionHandlingMiddleware>(); app.UseMiddleware<RequestLoggingMiddleware>(); app.UseCors(); app.UseAuthentication(); app.UseAuthorization(); app.MapControllers(). ExceptionHandlingMiddleware is the first UseMiddleware call, hence outer to every app-registered middleware and to the endpoint.

Code at stage-1: both the KeyNotFoundException and the ArgumentException clause call logger.LogWarning(ex, ...); only catch (Exception ex) calls logger.LogError(ex, "unhandled exception"). Nothing in ASP.NET Core imposes this mapping - it is three calls this class makes - so "this app's own convention" is exact.

Confirmed by execution today: the unhandled-exception stack trace of the test app ends at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Diagnostics.DeveloperExceptionPageMiddlewareImpl.Invoke(HttpContext context) - the dev page sits outside the app's own middleware - and the same run logged "The response has already started, the error page middleware will not be executed." issues.text: True but it stops one step early. Executed today (.NET 10.0.300, middleware that writes and flushes, then throws): the second exception came from this middleware's own `context.Response.StatusCode = statusCode` in WriteProblemAsync - Kestrel's HttpProtocol.set_StatusCode threw "StatusCode cannot be set because the response has already started".
